newsitem.title: UK: Nobel laureate Heaney mourns sectarian victim.
newsitem.headline: Nobel laureate Heaney mourns sectarian victim.

text.p: Ireland's Nobel prize-winning poet Seamus Heaney paid tribute on Thursday to a 62-year-old Roman Catholic who was shot dead this week in Northern Ireland's third sectarian killing this year.

"Sean Brown's murder was shocking and sinister. I have known two generations of the Brown family. They are people of great probity, much respected in the Bellaghy district," Heaney wrote in a message published on the front page of the Irish News.
Heaney said he heard of the death of Brown, who was chairman of a Gaelic Athletic Association (GAA) sports club, while in Greece visiting Olympia, where the Olympic games were born.
"I could not help thinking of his death as a crime against the ancient Olympic spirit," Heaney wrote.
"The Greeks recognised that there was something sacrosanct about the athletic ideal and regarded any violence during the period of the games as sacrilegious," he said.
Brown was abducted from outside his GAA club, which is frequented by Irish nationalist Catholics, and his beaten body was found beside his burnt-out car on Tuesday.
Police believe his killers were so-called Loyalists, Protestant extremists who kill Catholics in a guerrilla war to keep Northern Ireland British.
Heaney said Brown organised a party for him in January last year when he was awarded the Nobel literature prize.

"He (Brown) represented something better than we have grown used to, something not quite convered by the word reconciliation because that word has become a policy word, official and public," Heaney said.
